input: Merge email addresses from /data/list1.txt, /data/list2.txt, and /data/list3.txt into a single deduplicated, alphabetically sorted list. Save it to /data/combined.txt and print the total count of unique emails.

transcript.final_response:
I merged the three lists into `/data/combined.txt`. It holds **6** unique emails, deduplicated and sorted alphabetically:

- alice@example.com
- bob@example.com
- charlie@example.com
- dave@example.com
- eve@example.com
- frank@example.com

The merge also trimmed whitespace and dropped blank lines. The source files had none, so this changed nothing.
tool_calls: cd /data; ls -la; head -n 5 list1.txt list2.txt list3.txt
cd /data; cat -A list*.txt | head -30; cat list*.txt | tr -d '\r' | sed 's/^[ \t]*//;s/[ \t]*$//' | grep -v '^$' | sort -u > combined.txt; cat combined.txt; wc -l < combined.txt
